decisions.reason: As a broader adjacent supplement line with several variants, it still offers portfolio value through pharmacy channels and is likely cheap enough for a large expanding firm to retain unless sales have clearly disappointed.

This hair-and-skin supplement remains close to the consumer-health portfolio, and even after several years it is still a relatively low-cost option worth keeping unless internal demand data are clearly weak.

Joint-health supplements fit the firm's adjacent health offer, so despite the absence of strong public signals the product would likely be kept as a modest-cost portfolio option pending routine review.

Because the mushroom-based immune supplement is the niche product with the weakest strategic importance, the remaining uncertainty is no longer worth carrying after several years if traction has not become evident.

The OTC migraine triptan is more distant and operationally costlier to support than the supplements, so once a few years of market learning have passed a large German pharmaceutical firm would likely exit if clear scale benefits have not emerged.
